KO.rationale: Coca-Cola is a high-quality, defensive franchise with strong brand equity, a 64-year dividend increase streak, and an asset-light concentrate model supporting ~28% net margins and ~40% ROE. Q2 2025 showed solid sequential growth (revenue +12.6% QoQ, EPS +14.3% QoQ), and FY2025 results were strong ($47.9B revenue, EPS $3.04, +23% YoY). However, the stock is trading near the top of its 1-year P/E range (29.2x vs. 23.2-29.6x window), making it expensive vs. its own history. The India IPO plan for Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings (2027, $10B+ valuation) and the 2026 FIFA World Cup sponsorship are credible near-term catalysts that could unlock value and drive brand engagement. Risks include IRS tax litigation (potential $14B liability), GLP-1 drug headwinds to CSD demand, sugar taxes, and rising 10Y Treasury yields (4.45%) which compress multiples on defensive yield plays. The stock has already rallied ~22% from its 52-week low of $65.35, limiting upside. Net: solid franchise but stretched valuation caps the score modestly positive.
